//: Type-checking only. NOTHING IS COMPILED and nothing is emitted: the game is
served as the .js files you see, and `noEmit` below is what guarantees that
stays true. There are no .ts files here and there is no bundler.
WHY THIS EXISTS. The project's convention is JSDoc on every exported
function - what it does, units, and any invariant it assumes. Nothing
checked that the JSDoc still matched the code, and it had drifted: a
`@param` naming a parameter that no longer exists, `runRound`'s `@returns`
omitting two of the four things it returns, and several object params typed
narrower than the fields the body reads. A JSDoc that lies is the same
defect as a comment that lies, which this project treats as worse than dead
code because it reads as true.
WHY `ui/` IS NOT IN IT, which is a decision and not an oversight. Checking
it costs 303 errors against the engine side's 44, and almost all of them are
DOM typing - `Element` without `.focus`, `EventTarget` without `.closest` -
which is silenced with casts rather than fixed. And empirically it would buy
nothing: every interface defect found by playing this game has been visual
(contrast, overlapping rows) or behavioural (a tick that appeared too early,
a button that was missing). A type-checker sees none of those. The engine is
where a wrong type is a wrong number.
`tests/` is out for the same reason a test fixture is allowed to be a
half-built object on purpose.
